Subject: Storage partner stability sprint: prep and runbook gaps

Hi everyone,

Thanks for taking this on — we want to run a short "stability sprint" next week focused on operational runbooks and failure-mode alignment across index/storage providers (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector on S3). The goal is to reduce incident-to-recovery time for two common fault classes we saw in Q2: index corruption during re-ingest and cross-store read fallback spikes.

Proposed agenda (attached):
- 30m: shared incident review (recent customer cases)
- 45m: runbook alignment (re-ingest, TTL handling, cold-tier failover)
- 30m: handshake protocol + auth refresh (service accounts, token rotation)
- 15m: next steps and owners (SLAs, observability hooks)

Requests before the session:
- Partners: bring any short infra notes/limits (per-index QPS, recommended write-batching, snapshot cadence).
- Redwood: we'll bring our fallback policy doc and Prometheus alert map.

Can teams confirm a 60–90m block next Wed (Aug 12) or Thu (Aug 13) PST? We prefer Aug 12 morning. Calendar placeholder and a short runbook draft attached.

Appreciate it — this is high priority for several renewal customers and the SREs on both sides.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Partnerships (North America)
Redwood Inference

Rishi — thanks for the invite. We're in and can do Thu Aug 13 09:00–10:30 PST or Wed Aug 12 10:00–11:30 if that works better for Redwood.

Quick notes from Pinecone side (summary, see attached pinecone-infra-notes.md):
- Typical per-index QPS guidance: reserve headroom at 2.5x observed peak for re-ingest windows.
- Re-ingest best practice: chunk writes into 5–10k record batches and warm queries against a read-replica first.
- Snapshot cadence: daily snapshot + immediate post-re-ingest snapshot (helps fast restore).
- Known failure pattern: partial re-ingest + concurrent compaction can surface tombstone/dup keys; we recommend an explicit post-reindex validation step and a checksum exchange.

We'll bring a short 10-slide ops deck and one on-call playbook excerpt. Forwarding our infra notes (attached).

On auth: Pinecone can support short-lived tokens for cross-account replication; we'll show a sample rotation script.

Rishi — good framing. A couple quick asks from the ops team before the meeting:

1) Cost / throttling envelopes — can partners bring a short matrix of throttling behavior (graceful 429 patterns vs hard rejects) and any recommended backoff that we've seen work in prod? This matters for our mid-tier customers.

2) Observability hooks — we need exact metric names (or example PromQL) for read-latency, index-ingest-latency, and failed-lookup rates. If Pinecone/Weaviate can paste those in the doc we'll wire them into our dashboards ahead of the session.

3) Failover semantics — call out how the provider recommends preserving strong/ eventual consistency during fallback to S3/pgvector. If we can't preserve strong consistency, we need a recommended user-visible message pattern to surface degraded guarantees.

We're blocking Aug 12 10:00–11:30 PST internally; if partners prefer Aug 13 Alex suggested that's fine — please confirm. Also tagging Laura for runbook ownership and Ben for commercial implications.

Thanks — Vanessa
